\caption{Seven MIPLIB-derived instances whose high point relaxation is exactly the MIPLIB model they were built from (checked in exact arithmetic by \texttt{scripts/compare\_hpr.py}), so the published MIPLIB optimum (MIPLIB 2017's solution file) is a lower bound; a verified bilevel feasible point at that value is optimal by accepted benchmark conventions. The MIPLIB optima are floating-point results of MILP solvers (class (ii) of Section~\ref{app:classes}), not exact-arithmetic proofs: the objectives of noswot, ex10 and neos-1445765 take integer values only (integer coefficients on integer variables), and those of pigeon-10 multiples of 1,000 only, so their published bounds round up to $-41$, $100$, $-17{,}783$ and $-9{,}000$ and the results are safe if those bounds are valid; for timtab1 the agreement of point and bound is numerical. BOBILib: the instance's status before this work. Lefebvre and Schmidt's run files also report ex10\_0\_100 optimal at 100; their paper does not state it, so it is not counted as published. (neos-950242\_0\_100 meets its bound too, but was already listed as optimal in an earlier BOBILib release and is counted as published.)}\label{tab:hpr}\\
